disposition_reason: Table 2 prints mean, median, min and max for 30 elements in 35 counterfeit whisky products (new data); the 170 authentic samples reprint the companion 2022 paper and are not re-extracted.

study.design: Authenticity study comparing 35 counterfeit whisky products with 170 authentic whiskies
study.origin: Counterfeits from 9 anonymous sources (producers or places of manufacture), distributed as whisky analogs; authentic set as in the companion paper
study.method: Microwave HNO3 digestion; ICP-MS, ICP-OES, CV-AAS for Hg (as in companion paper 10.3390/foods11111616)
lod: Not printed; validation as in the companion paper
study.qa: Validation procedures as in the companion paper; not reported here

controls.control: Counterfeit (unaged or briefly aged) vs authentic whisky
controls.outcome: Median Ni 39.86 vs 12.96 µg/L, Sr 53.72 vs 45.81, S 14,679 vs 4648 µg/L higher in fakes; Cu median 56.86 vs 216.0 µg/L lower in fakes; significant for Be, Ca, Cu, Li, Mg, Mo, S, Sn, Sr

unresolved: Table 3 'A' rows (170 authentic whiskies) reprint the companion paper gajek2022-whisky-elemental-fingerprints-type-age-origin and are not extracted here.
Cu mean differs between Table 2 (2383) and Table 3 (4021 µg/L); text prints the maximum as 33.21 µg/L.
Table 3 prints Mg SD 764 for fakes and 13,926 for authentic, which look transposed or misprinted.
Per-sample values not published; source codes S1-S9 not linked to sample codes except F10-F12.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Polish maximum levels for high-percentage alcohols
regulatory_or_exposure.value: Pb 0.3 mg/L, Cd 0.03 mg/L; Cd exceeded in 3 of 35 counterfeits (32.25-65.90 µg/L), Pb not exceeded
